items.claim: Rafael gives Q1 2026 revenue guidance range of $4.32B-$4.68B.
items.quote: We expect TI revenue in the range of $4.32 billion to $4.68
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Rafael gives Q1 2026 EPS guidance range of $1.22-$1.48.
items.quote: earnings per share to be in the range of $1.22 to $1.48
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Rafael reiterates FY2026 effective tax rate guidance of about 13%-14%.
items.quote: our effective tax rate for 2026 to be about 13% to 14%.
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Q4 gross margin was 56% of revenue, down 150bps sequentially.
items.quote: gross profit margin decreased 150 basis points.
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Rafael tells analysts to assume opex up low-single-digits when modeling Q1 gross margin.
items.quote: assume OpEx is up low single digits
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI raised its quarterly dividend per share by 4% to $1.42.
items.quote: We also increased our dividend per share by 4%
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI highlights this dividend increase marks its 22nd consecutive year of dividend increases.
items.quote: marking our 22nd consecutive year of dividend increases
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI returned $6.5B to shareholders via dividends and buybacks over the trailing 12 months.
items.quote: we have returned $6.5 billion in the past 12 months
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: 2026 gross CapEx reaffirmed at $2B-$3B, unchanged from prior guidance.
items.quote: We continue to expect CapEx for 2026 between $2 billion and
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Investment tax credit (ITC) rate on 2026 capex investments rises to 35% effective January 1, 2026.
items.quote: it is now 35% as of January 1 of '26.
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Haviv credits TI's BCP power process technology, built in Sherman, for serving the data center VCORE/voltage-rail opportunity.
items.quote: This is where our BCP process is serving us very well there.
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: The high-power data center rail product is currently sampling, with management expecting the opportunity to expand further.
items.quote: That product is sampling, and we expect our opportunity in
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Haviv flags unexplained recent order 'noise,' loosely tying it to issues at a certain supplier and to memory shortages elsewhere.
items.quote: we have seen some noise in the last several months
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Haviv admits he cannot explain what is driving the recent industrial order pickup and says its durability remains unproven.
items.quote: I can't tell you why. We'll have to see how it plays out.
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: TI notes it transacts most revenue direct with customers rather than through a distribution channel, giving it real-time demand visibility.
items.quote: we transact most of our revenue direct with our customers
items.speaker: Mike Beckman

items.claim: Management describes a recurring pattern over the past several quarters of customers placing urgent, just-in-time orders.
items.quote: customers wanting to come in, want product quickly.
items.speaker: Mike Beckman

items.claim: Analyst Vivek Arya asks whether peers' announced 2026 price increases are contributing to TI's above-seasonal Q1 guide.
items.quote: there is some discussion about price increases from some of
items.speaker: Vivek Arya

items.claim: Haviv states that TI's above-seasonal Q1 guidance is not driven by price increases, contrasting with peers raising prices.
items.quote: the answer is no, it's not pricing related.
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Haviv reaffirms the Sherman fab buildout is ahead of schedule with high yields.
items.quote: we are very pleased about the execution in Sherman
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Haviv commits to continued progress on the 45-nanometer technology transition at Lehi, mainly supporting the automotive radar business.
items.quote: we are busy with our 45-nanometer technology, mainly
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

qa_flags.question: Chris Caso (Wolfe Research) asks if there are any plans in place now to increase factory loadings, and what would need to be seen to take that step.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Rafael declines to disclose the direction of loadings ('We are not making any disclosure right now on which way the loadings are going'), stating only that nothing significant has changed versus Q4.

qa_flags.question: William Stein (Truist) asks if TI would be able to disclose the book-to-bill ratio behind the strong bookings commentary.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Mike Beckman declines to give a specific book-to-bill figure ('I don't have a number specifically to provide you for what bookings did'), redirecting to qualitative end-market commentary instead.

qa_flags.question: Timothy Arcuri (UBS) asks whether 2026 CapEx could fall as low as ~$1 billion (below 5% of revenue) next year, referencing a prior comment from a December conference.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Neither Haviv nor Rafael confirms or denies the ~$1B floor figure; Haviv reframes the answer around a generic 'maintenance capex' concept and Rafael answers with a capital-intensity formula (about 1.2x long-term revenue growth) rather than addressing the specific low-end number asked about.
